target_customer: Flexitarian and vegan consumers and restaurants buying premium plant-based whole cut steaks
problem: Plant-based meat mostly imitates ground products; whole cuts with real texture and marbling were missing, limiting meat reduction.
business_model: Consumer packaged food sold through direct online sales, retailers and restaurants

technical_complexity.rationale: Proprietary protein texturing (a reverse grinder style process) to mimic muscle fibre and fat marbling at scale is hard food-tech engineering for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Texturing know-how is hard to copy quickly, but several rivals pursued whole cuts and large meat firms could follow.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents focused on ground products at the time; later coverage lists many whole cut entrants but no sign of acquisition of Juicy Marbles.

market_need_then: Plant-based meat demand was high in 2020 and 2021, and the company reported selling 100,000 steaks around the Valentine's Day 2023 run up per trade coverage.

identity.visual_style: Not verified; company site could not be fetched (safety check rate-limited)

branding.brand_signature: Name that evokes meat marbling, applied to a plant-based steak
branding.community_and_virality: Trade press (TechCrunch, Food Dive, Green Queen, SingularityHub) covered the filet mignon and Waitrose launch.

brand_strength.rationale: Repeated trade and tech press coverage and a Waitrose listing suggest a recognisable niche brand, but no brand specific sources were found.

outcome_analysis: Juicy Marbles launched a plant-based filet mignon in 2021, raised a $4.5M seed from World Fund in November 2021, and later reached retail listings such as Waitrose in 2023. No later rounds, exit or shutdown were found, so it is an active company whose funding history after the seed is not public in the sources checked.
